title: Concurrence Launches AI Agents to Automate Hospital Patient Care and Intake
summary:
AI startup Concurrence has debuted a platform called Superintelligent Care that provides hospitals with autonomous agents to manage clinician instructions for patients. The system handles care plans from medication checks and pharmacy communications to follow-up appointments, while keeping all patient data on the hospital's local servers and requiring doctors to make all final medical decisions.

The startup, previously known as Amigo, designed the agents to gather medical histories and current symptoms via voice or text before a patient's visit. A clinical team using the technology at a cancer survivorship program reported that the automated summaries reduced the time spent on manual patient intake by more than 80%.

selectedTweets.text:
Finally, a solution for one of the largest problems in healthcare: Over 80% less time spent on manual patient intake. That's what a clinical team reports from using Concurrence.

Its AI agent collects patient histories, symptoms and medications over voice or text before the appointment. Clinicians get a summary in the medical record before they see the patient.

For people navigating life after cancer treatment, the agent also provides support between visits, with urgent situations escalated to a human clinician.

I'd rather spend an appointment discussing treatment and asking questions than repeating a medication list that could have been collected beforehand. Seriously amazing.
